stances.note: Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) has not written its reading of Rwanda; the atlas mirrors Rwanda's 'adversary' reading as 'adversary' at low confidence, on the same evidence. Bond and trend are not assessed from this side.

stances_toward.note: Adversary, the one mortal enemy in the ontology's sense: Kigali's declared aim is the group's elimination, and it is the stated casus belli for the 'defensive measures' in the Congo (foreign ministry, 10 Dec 2025; Rwanda's ambassador at the Security Council, Mar 2026; Kagame, Apr 2026). The Accords make FDLR neutralisation a Congolese obligation and the US presses Kinshasa on it (13 Oct 2026; 120+ ex-combatants and family repatriated with UN support). How strong the FDLR still is, and how deep inside the Congolese army and the Wazalendo militias, is disputed: the UN experts accuse Kinshasa of relying on them and Rwandan-aligned commentary says the group is embedded in the Congolese security structures, while critics say Kigali inflates the threat to justify its presence. Bond grievance: founded by remnants of the 1994 perpetrators.

relations_to.summary: Eliminate the FDLR, the group founded by remnants of the 1994 perpetrators, as a threat on the border: Kigali's stated casus belli, written into the Washington Accords as a Congolese obligation ('neutralise') against which Rwandan disengagement is measured; the US pressed Kinshasa on it on 13 Oct 2026 and noted 120+ ex-combatants and family repatriated with UN help.
